title: CI CD builds tests artifacts deployment and rollback
concepts: Continuous integration integrates small changes frequently and validates each candidate. Continuous delivery keeps a releasable artifact ready; continuous deployment automatically releases changes that pass the chosen controls.

A pipeline should make dependencies explicit: checkout, deterministic dependency resolution, build, test, package, provenance, publish, deploy, verify, and recover. A green pipeline proves only the checks it actually ran.

Build once and promote the same immutable artifact through environments so deployment does not silently rebuild different bits. Artifacts are retained outputs for later jobs or inspection; caches are disposable performance aids and must not hold secrets.

Deployment strategies trade release speed, infrastructure cost, and rollback behavior. Rolling, blue-green, canary, and progressive delivery require health signals and database changes that tolerate overlap between old and new application versions.

GitHub Actions jobs receive only explicitly granted GITHUB_TOKEN permissions. Third-party actions are executable dependencies; pin immutable action revisions or verified dependency lockfiles, and use narrowly scoped OIDC federation rather than long-lived cloud credentials where supported.

Automatic rollback needs a defined failure signal, a known prior artifact, and compatible state changes. Reverting application bits cannot automatically reverse irreversible data migrations or external side effects.

versionNotes.edition: GitHub Actions current workflow syntax, checked 2026-11-14
items: GitHub Actions workflow syntax now supports timezone-aware `schedule` entries and concurrency queue policies beyond the original single-pending behavior. Hosted runner images and action runtime versions change independently; manifests must not freeze an unverified image label as a timeless guarantee.
